summary: Routing to an outdated quantized model variant causing elevated p95/p99 latency and sporadic timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports increased p95/p99 latency (up to 6s) and occasional request timeouts (HTTP 504) since 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC. Root cause appears to be requests routed to an older quantized variant that is in a cold state and triggers expensive cold-starts + slower quantized execution paths.

Impact:
- NovaHealth production workloads experience degraded user-facing latency and sporadic 504s across several endpoints.
- Customer reports elevated error rates during morning traffic ramp (us-east).
- Affects mission-critical inference for clinical decision support; customer flagged as dedicated tenant and requested urgent investigation.

Environment:
- Customer: NovaHealth (dedicated pool)
- Region: prod us-east
- Deployed variants: redwood/llama-3-70b-v2 (primary), redwood/llama-3-70b-quantized-v1 (fallback)
- Traffic pattern: steady ramp 08:00-10:00 local, spikes to 250 rps

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send sustained generation requests at 200-250 rps to the customer's route (route id provided in ticket attachments).
2) Observe increased p95/p99 and occasional 504s between 09:00-10:30 UTC.
3) On our side, confirm that requests intermittently land on quantized-v1 variant.

Logs & traces (collected):
- Trace IDs: trace-20260310-9a1b, trace-20260310-9a2c (attached).
- API gateway logs show 504s with upstream timeout to serving-runtime at 09:15 UTC.
- Router decision logs indicate a fallback policy triggered due to perceived capacity shortage; selected variant: redwood/llama-3-70b-quantized-v1.
- Serving runtime allocation timestamps show container spin-up and long model load times for quantized-v1 (~2.4s additional latency before first token).

Initial hypothesis:
1) Fallback routing policy incorrectly prefers an older quantized variant when capacity signals are transient, not accounting for the quantized variant's cold-start overhead.
2) Quantized-v1 lacks warm cache for KV/collapsed attention paths and has slower kernel-path for this customer's sequence-length distribution causing p99 spikes.
3) Autoscale decision loop may have been slower than expected during the morning ramp, causing router to fall back to variant that was technically compatible but performance-degraded.

Investigation notes:
- Confirmed router logs show a capacity mismatch signal from the dedicated pool between 09:12-09:18 UTC.
- Node-level metrics: GPU utilization was at ~62% on primary pool, but several nodes were being drained for housekeeping; autoscaler not yet provisioned additional capacity.
- Quantized-v1 model artifact was last promoted to prod in Dec 2025 and was not included in the latest kernel selection benchmark; lacks a warmup image.
- Trace analysis shows first-token latency contributed ~2.2s for requests routed to quantized-v1; non-quantized variant first-token latency ~0.3s.
- Customer confirmed they had pinned rollouts to allow fallback to quantized-v1 for cost reasons previously.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Support temporarily adjusted routing policy for NovaHealth to prefer primary (non-quantized) variant for 1 hour while autoscaler capacity was increased.
- Triggered a rapid warmup job for quantized-v1 in the customer's dedicated pool to pre-load model artifacts.
- Eng SRE patched router scoring to weight cold-start penalty for known quantized artifacts (hotfix deployed to canary 2026-03-11).

Remaining action items:
- SRE/Infra: add warmup orchestration for quantized variants during traffic ramps (ticket INT-412).
- Runtime: add metadata to model catalog that includes estimated cold-start penalty to guide routing.
- Product: create customer-facing doc explaining fallback tradeoffs for quantized variants and recommended pinning strategies.
- Postmortem: link to incident page and finalize by 2026-03-18.

Next steps for customer communication:
- Confirm with NovaHealth that temporary routing change improved latency (requested they monitor 2026-03-12 morning ramp).
- Share planned timeline for warmup orchestration and router scoring changes.

Expected resolution criteria:
- No routing to cold quantized variants during peak traffic without warmup; p99 latency returns to baseline for >=72 hours.

investigation_notes: Router fallback policy selected quantized-v1 due to transient capacity signal; quantized-v1 has large cold-start penalty not previously modeled. Autoscaler lag + node drain created a temporary shortage. Confirmed with traces and model load timing.
resolution_notes: Temporary routing override applied, warmup job executed, hotfix to add cold-start penalty weighting deployed to canary. Remaining work tracked in INT-412 and a product doc story. Customer confirmed improvement.
resolution: Workaround applied and hotfix deployed. Ongoing work to prevent recurrence; ticket will be updated with postmortem link once complete.
